tob-13138: E. A. Wallis Budge’s translation of the Egyptian Book of the Dead presents the spells the pharaohs’ scribes wrote to carry the dead safely into the next world. Readers meet the gods of the judgment hall, the monsters that threaten the traveler, and the magic words that turn them aside. It is our clearest window onto the religion of the Nile three thousand years ago.
tob-13338: Paramahansa Yogananda’s autobiography brought Indian yoga to the West when it appeared in 1946. He recounts his training under his guru Sri Yukteswar, his encounters with saints and sages, and his mission to carry meditation to America. Part memoir, part spiritual adventure, it has introduced millions of readers to the inner life of India.
tob-0138: John Robison’s 1797 alarm-bell warned that the Illuminati, though banned on paper, lived on as a hidden hand behind Europe’s overturnings. The Edinburgh teacher drew on his lodge ties and German word to paint his frightening scene. Few books have done more to plant the thought of secret masters tugging history’s strings.
tob-0038: In 1975 the Senate’s Church Committee dragged into daylight the CIA’s murder plots against foreign rulers — Castro, Lumumba, Trujillo, and more. This interim report details the poisons, the mob go-betweens, and the presidents’ deniability. The findings shook America and remade spy-oversight.
tob-4138: Waite’s gathering of Paracelsus’s Hermes-and-gold writings — the Swiss leech-rebel who overturned healing and wonder-craft alike in the 1500s. This first volume opens his vast hard writings to English readers. The master’s fire blazes on every page, with Waite’s notes to light the way.
cia-0000112338: Take 1 of 2 — a January 1991 foreign press note on the USSR, catalogued under a bureaucratic code. These numbered takes were running summaries of what Soviet newspapers were saying as the union fell apart. The document is one installment of the daily effort to read a collapsing empire through its own press.
cia-0000112838: A September 1946 file on Robert Donald Chisholm, charged with treason. Treason — betraying one's own country — was the gravest accusation in the book. Dated a year after the war, the entry shows the long tail of wartime betrayals still being processed.
cia-0000119738: The Hungarian situation as of 1:00 AM Eastern Daylight Time — another overnight wire in the crisis series. While America slept, analysts kept the watch, summarizing Budapest's night for the morning brief. The entry is vigilance as routine — the revolution never paused, so neither did the reporting.
cia-0000124338: An estimated July 1952 military file on biological warfare and atomic weapons — the truncated subject suggests a survey of unconventional arms. In the Korean War's darkest phase, every weapon was on the table. The entry is a reminder of how close the unthinkable felt.
cia-0000132238: Situation Report 555: Where is Saddam? — the truncated title asks the question outright. The dictator had vanished into his bunkers, and his whereabouts were intelligence gold. The entry is the hunt for one man: the war's most wanted, underground.
cia-0000132338: A May 1959 NSC briefing covering the Caribbean, Argentina, and Iraq — three crises, one sitting. The National Security Council juggled the world's troubles in a single meeting. The document is the Cold War's breadth: three continents, one afternoon.
cia-0000132638: A May 1960 report: Nicaragua suspending relations with Cuba. Somoza's Nicaragua was among the first to cut ties with revolutionary Havana. The document is the rupture: the dictatorship, disowning the revolution.
cia-0000132738: A 1961 roundup: the anti-Castro group, international contacts, the economy, and Cuba at the UN. Four lenses on the island. The document is the composite: the opposition, the diplomacy, the money, and the podium.
cia-0000135738: An estimated 1961 Spanish-language 2506 Brigade document — the archive's dating says estmated. Another page from the brigade's files. The document is the fragment: the invasion's paper trail, continuing.
cia-0000136138: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on destroying rail targets. The railways were the invasion's first objective. The document is the order: the rails, destroyed.
cia-0000136338: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN advising to proceed with the present plan — LINCOLN not optimistic, the truncated title suggests. The order came with doubt attached. The document is the paradox: proceed, but without hope.
cia-0000136938: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on purchasing eight P-47 fighters — and suggestions, the truncated title adds. The air force, bought. The document is the purchase: the fighters, eight.
cia-0000139038: An estimated 1966 document on the Greek junta's plans for Andreas Papandreou — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The colonels eyed the opposition leader. The document is the plan: the target, marked.
cia-0000141138: A 1960 cable from Guatemala with a personnel strength report listing names and job titles — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The roster. The document is the report: the staff, listed.
un-ga-res-38: General Assembly Resolution 38, from 1946. Each early resolution was a precedent — the young UN learning to speak. The entry records the number and year; the full text records what was said.
un-ga-res-a-69-38: Resolution A/69/38, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The modern Assembly deciding. The designation and year are certain; the subject is in the text.
un-ga-res-58-238: Resolution 58/238, adopted in 2004 during the 58th session — aligned. The designation and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-138: Security Council Resolution 138, adopted in June 1960 — the Eichmann resolution, declaring that Israel's abduction of Adolf Eichmann from Argentina violated Argentine sovereignty and requesting appropriate reparation. The Council weighed justice against the law of nations — and chose the law. The resolution is the rebuke: the kidnapping, condemned.
un-sc-res-238: Security Council Resolution 238, adopted in 1967. The Council deliberated. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1038: Security Council Resolution 1038, cataloged with the year 1992 — the numbering belongs to 1996, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1438: Security Council Resolution 1438, adopted in October 2002 — the Bali bombings resolution, condemning the terrorist attacks that killed over 200 people in Indonesia. The Council answered the atrocity with unanimous censure. The resolution is the condemnation: the bombings, denounced.
un-sc-res-1738: Security Council Resolution 1738, cataloged with the year 1977 — though the well-known journalists-protection resolution of that number belongs to 2006, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted — and the subject is left to the text.
un-sc-res-2338: Security Council Resolution 2338, cataloged with the year 1989 — the numbering suggests 2017, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
cia-0000135838: A 1952 CIA file titled Central American Situation, numbered 0000135838. The isthmus two years before the Guatemala coup. The document is the situation: the region, 1952.
cia-0000136638: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136638. The Bay of Pigs force, documented in its own tongue. The entry is the tongue: the Spanish, primary.
cia-0000136738: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136738, date approximate. The circa set. The entry is the circa: the dating, soft.
plos-pone-0000038: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper on efficient non-viral ocular gene transfer with compacted DNA nanoparticles — the truncated title cuts off the rest. Gene therapy for eyes, delivered without viruses. The paper is the delivery: the genes, to the eye — no virus needed.
un-sc-res-738: Security Council Resolution 738, adopted in 1992 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d38: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 5, 1943 — Document 38. A second letter the same day. The message is the second: the day, doubled.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d138: The minister in Egypt, Kirk, to the Secretary of State, November 18, 1943 — Document 138. Cairo's reporting continued. The cable is the continuation: Kirk, briefing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d238: Minutes of the president's meeting with the Joint Chiefs of Staff, November — the truncated title cuts off the day — Document 238. The war council, minuted. The minutes are the council: the chiefs, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d338: The Secretary of War Stimson to the Assistant Secretary of War McCloy — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 338. The boss answered his deputy. The memo is the answer: Stimson, to McCloy.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d438: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, December 4, 1943 — Document 438. The planners met on. The minutes are the continuation: the chiefs, conferring.
arxiv-2605-08838: Chatbots that look up documents before answering — retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG — are usually tested on benchmarks that may have leaked into their training data, inflating the scores. Jiayi Liu, Jiaxing Zhang, Bowen Jin, and Jennifer Neville propose a method for generating leakage-free benchmarks, so RAG systems face genuinely unseen questions. The 2026 paper is about honest evaluation of AI assistants.
arxiv-2605-08938: Neural networks that stand in for physics simulators are fast but unproven — can we formally verify they behave? Ali Baheri and Ignacio Laguna Peralta compile small Fourier neural operators into SMT formulas, letting automated solvers check their properties. The 2026 paper asks whether AI surrogates for PDEs can carry mathematical guarantees.
arxiv-2605-09038: Language models with web access still search clumsily, firing off naive queries. Hu Jinchao, Meizhi Zhong, Kehai Chen, and Min Zhang teach them better with SearchSkill: an evolving bank of search skills the model learns to use. The 2026 paper trains AI to research like a pro.
arxiv-2605-09138: Quantum channels carry quantum information, and symmetry can push their capacity thresholds higher. Avantika Agarwal, Amolak Ratan Kalra, Sungjai Lee, and colleagues derive enhanced thresholds from symmetry considerations. The 2026 paper is quantum information theory on how symmetry raises what channels can carry.
arxiv-2605-09738: Eisenstein series are modular forms with deep arithmetic; their lacunary recurrences and 2-adic properties hide real secrets. Liubomir Chiriac and Andrei Jorza investigate these hidden patterns with great care and precision. The 2026 paper brings deep number theory to beautiful classical objects.
plos-pone-0003438: Behavioral ecologists tested foragers on level ground, literally, in this 2008 paper. When a landscape holds equal risk everywhere, animals still must decide where to eat, and classic models of risk-sensitive choice were put to the test. The experiments in these risk-uniform landscapes clarified how animals balance food gains against danger when danger does not vary.
plos-pone-0003538: Microbiologists peered inside Salmonella's hideout in this 2008 paper. The bacterium replicates within a membrane bubble in host cells, and the team depleted two lysosomal membrane proteins, LAMP-1 and LAMP-2, to see what happens. The vacuole's fate without them reveals how the pathogen exploits the cell's own compartments.
plos-pone-0003638: In 2008, a team looked at how young muscle cells build podosomes, tiny feet that help cells grip and move. Three players teamed up to build them: dystroglycan, Tks5, and the Src protein. The work shows how young muscle cells grip their ground, a step that breaks down in some muscle illness.
plos-pone-0003738: In 2008, Jensen, Martin-Gronert, and Storgaard linked small birth size to altered muscle signaling. Young men born with low birth weight showed changed PI3-kinase and Akt signaling in skeletal muscle, a pathway tied to insulin action. The finding traces adult diabetes risk back to the womb.
plos-pone-0003838: In 2008, Cremer, Ugelvig, and Drijfhout asked what makes garden ants conquer new lands. Comparing invasive and stay-at-home species, they tested whether success comes from old adaptations or new tricks. The study probes the roots of invasiveness in six-legged colonizers.
plos-pone-0003938: In 2008, Gomez-Nunez, Haro, and Dao built light-triggered tools for immunology. Their non-natural, photo-reactive amino acids act as probes that snap into action under light. The team aimed the probes at WT1, a protein overexpressed in leukemias. The light-switched amino acids open new ways to study immune targets.
plos-pone-0004038: In 2008, Swoap and Weinshenker found one chemical running mouse hibernation both ways. Norepinephrine controlled both the start of torpor and the waking from it. Entry into torpor and exit from it used distinct mechanisms under one chemical's command. The finding maps the brain chemistry of an extreme energy-saving state.
plos-pone-0004138: In 2009, Peters, Simmons, and Rhodes tested shifting tastes in faces and bodies. Women's preference for masculine and symmetric male faces varied across the menstrual cycle. The fertile phase tilted taste toward masculinity. The pattern feeds debate on evolved mate choice.
plos-pone-0004238: In 2009, Langmesser, Franken, and Feil tied a signaling enzyme to mouse sleep. cGMP-dependent protein kinase type I shaped sleep timing and quality both. Mice lacking the kinase slept quite differently. The pathway links nitric oxide signaling to healthy nightly rest.
plos-pone-0004338: In 2009, Milstein, Mormann, and Fried found static hiding in brain waves. Human brain recordings showed shot noise and Brownian 1/f-squared behavior. The ubiquitous pattern traced to neuronal firing. The finding grounds brain-signal theory. The work links single spikes to field recordings.
plos-pone-0358738: Maggots clean wounds — an old medical trick with real science behind it. This paper chemically dissects extracts from Hemipyrellia ligurriens fly larvae, mapping their proteins and fats with advanced lab instruments. The team flagged candidate antimicrobial molecules, hunting for the natural antibiotics that let larvae thrive in filth without getting infected.
plos-pone-0358538: Teaching AI to spot anomalies frame-by-frame needs expensive labels. This paper learned the interactions instead: weakly supervised video anomaly detection built on human-object interactions. By watching how people handle objects, the system flags the unusual with far less labeling.
plos-pone-0358038: Muscles grow when myoblasts fuse — and the Tceal7 gene helps drive the process. This paper showed Tceal7 is a BRG1-regulated target of calcineurin signaling that promotes myoblast differentiation. The regulatory chain adds a concrete piece to the puzzle of how muscles build and repair themselves.
plos-pone-0334738: Emotions spread between people like rhythms — and mathematics can model the beat. This paper built a dynamical systems model of emotional contagion with oscillatory coupling in the circumplex of affect. The equations show how moods synchronize between individuals, much like coupled oscillators falling into step with each other.
plos-pone-0355938: What makes a psychology manuscript look high-quality to peer reviewers? This study tested the effect of manuscript characteristics on quality assessment of scientific manuscripts in psychology. The findings expose which surface features — writing flair, formatting, framing — sway peer judgment apart from the science itself.
plos-pone-0358338: Touch in physical education teaching is fraught — especially across genders. This cross-sectional questionnaire study surveyed women’s discomfort with physical contact in PE, broken down by the initiator’s gender and relationship. The findings guide concrete policies for respectful, effective coaching.
plos-pone-0356638: Hepatitis B can trigger catastrophic acute liver failure with little warning. This paper identified and validated oxidative stress-related immune signatures in HBV-associated acute liver failure using WGCNA network analysis and machine learning. The signatures could one day guide urgent, life-saving treatment decisions.
plos-pone-0357038: Revascularizing blocked leg arteries should restore patients’ ability to move — but does it? This paper studied functional capacity improvement and subsequent cardiovascular events after lower extremity revascularization. The outcomes measure the real-world benefit patients actually feel.
plos-pone-0353938: Crop yield predictions are only as trustworthy as the data feeding them. This paper tested how sensitive machine learning regression models are to data structure and quality in crop yield prediction. The findings warn modelers — and the farmers relying on them — about which data flaws distort forecasts most.
plos-pone-0356138: Do diabetes drugs protect the aging brain — or harm it? This retrospective cohort study examined antidiabetic medications and the risk of cognitive disorders in type 2 diabetes. The findings help doctors choose glucose-lowering drugs with the brain in mind, not just blood sugar.
plos-pone-0355238: Teaching machines to hear emotion in speech demands fusing multiple signal types. This paper combined hybrid CNN-embedding fusion with MFCC-SVM for speech emotion recognition, testing random versus actor-wise evaluation on the CREMA-D dataset. The honest evaluation comparison exposes how easily emotion AI fools itself.
plos-pone-0356238: Predicting which viruses infect which bacteria — phage-host interactions — unlocks microbiome medicine. FusionPHI is an attention-driven multi-modal feature fusion network for that prediction. The model’s fused features outperform simpler approaches, accelerating phage therapy development.
plos-pone-0356838: Dengue’s aftermath may include lingering cardiovascular damage — but the evidence is scattered. This paper published a protocol for a systematic review of post-acute and long-term cardiovascular effects following dengue infection. The planned synthesis will determine whether dengue survivors’ hearts need long-term watching.
plos-pone-0345338: Fatty liver threatens the vasculature — but can quickly shedding liver fat reverse the damage? This paper examined the impact of short-term hepatic triglyceride reduction on vascular health in adults with or at risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. The findings test whether the liver’s recovery translates into healthier blood vessels.
plos-pone-0355838: Breast cancer risk prediction could get personal — by simulating each woman’s signaling pathways. This paper integrated dynamic pathway modeling with subject-specific transcriptomic data to assess risk. The personalized simulations promise risk estimates tuned to individual biology rather than population averages.
plos-pone-0350938: Funding agencies struggle to choose among worthy research proposals. This paper built a peer-review decision support tool using the analytic hierarchy process. The structured tool brings consistency to funding decisions — helping public money flow to the science that merits it most.
plos-pone-0349838: Thyroid eye disease — bulging, inflamed eyes — needs objective measures of activity. This paper identified orbital CT biomarkers for assessing disease activity. The imaging biomarkers give ophthalmologists numbers to guide treatment — replacing subjective judgment with quantifiable orbital changes.
plos-pone-0355338: Measuring body composition in anesthetized dogs — via multifrequency bioimpedance — depends on electrode choice. This paper compared clip and needle electrodes. The comparison guides veterinary anesthesiologists toward measurements they can trust during surgery.
plos-pone-0355738: Post-activation performance enhancement — priming jumps with heavy lifts — may differ by sex. This paper tested its effects on countermovement jumps in men and women. The sex-comparative findings help coaches program priming strategies that actually work for each athlete.
plos-pone-0354238: Long COVID patients’ quality of life varies — and functional somatic disorder diagnoses may explain some of it. This cross-sectional study examined health-related quality of life according to that diagnostic presence. The findings untangle how overlapping labels shape patients’ lived experience of persistent illness.
europmc-pmc2792038: Mice were used in this 2009 study to test whether a specific set of immune cells, Th1-Th17 cells, can protect against two very different infections: Staphylococcus aureus bacteria and Candida albicans fungus. The experiments show these cells mount a defense that works against both pathogens. The result points toward vaccines that train this arm of immunity.
europmc-pmc2820538: Aging cells broadcast inflammatory signals, and this 2010 paper shows mice share the human version. The authors demonstrate that a human-like senescence-associated secretory phenotype is conserved in mouse cells, as long as oxygen levels stay physiological. The cross-species match validates mice as models for studying aging. It also flags oxygen as a key experimental detail.
europmc-pmc2867938: Much of the genome's chatter happens outside genes, and this 2010 paper maps it. The authors show a large share of extragenic RNA pol II transcription sites overlap enhancers, the genome's switches. Their finding tied stray transcription to regulation. The work reframed genomic noise as potential signal.
europmc-pmc2998438: A whiff of cell exhaust extends worm life. This 2010 paper shows a mild burst of mitochondrial oxidants lengthens life in roundworms. The authors flip the free-radical story. Their work reframes aging biology. Small stresses seem to toughen the animal.
europmc-pmc3017038: Wnt signals light up in living mouse embryos. This 2010 paper builds a bright reporter that shows Wnt activity cell by cell. The authors watch development glow in real time. Their tool spread through labs. Cancer researchers track rogue Wnt with it.
europmc-pmc3035538: A gut parasite may jump between animals and people. This 2003 paper fingerprints Giardia strains with a metabolic gene to trace animal-to-human spread. The authors reveal the strain map. Their work informs water safety. Beavers famously carry it into streams.
europmc-pmc3069738: Protein crystallography got its bible. This 2011 paper tours the CCP4 software suite and its newest tools. The authors survey the toolkit. Their overview trained crystallographers. The suite is free for academics. Thousands of structures came from it. The bible gets updated every few years.
europmc-pmc3084838: Antibodies eased Lewy body disease in mice. This 2011 paper shows antibody shots reduce brain and behavior damage in Parkinson-like mice. The authors' result backs immune therapy. Their work points to human trials. The shots cleared toxic protein clumps. Human antibody trials followed the lead.
europmc-pmc6511038: Part one of the Japan Esophageal Society's 2017 guidelines for esophageal cancer care. Japan's doctors have deep experience with this disease, and these recommendations distill it into standard practice. Clinicians get step-by-step guidance on diagnosis, staging, and the first treatment decisions, so patients receive consistent, up-to-date care.
europmc-pmc6528438: Doctors' notes hold a wealth of information about chronic disease, but it is buried in free text. This systematic review surveys natural language processing methods that mine clinical notes for diagnoses, symptoms, and outcomes. The techniques promise to turn everyday medical records into research data - while wrestling with messy handwriting, abbreviations, and privacy.
europmc-pmc6591438: Asthma touches all ages but wears different faces in children and adults. This review distills the epidemiology: how common it is, what drives it - from air pollution to genes - and how its course differs across life. The patterns guide prevention and care for a disease that still kills in its severe forms.
europmc-pmc6685538: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis - the two faces of inflammatory bowel disease - still guard their secrets. This review covers diagnosis, prevention, and treatment: what triggers the gut's civil war and how doctors calm it. Though the ultimate cause stays mysterious, the therapeutic arsenal keeps growing.
europmc-pmc6699738: Gut microbes are tenants we can evict or encourage - and the host does both. This review surveys what shapes microbiota composition: diet, drugs, age, and the body's own signals like microRNAs. Understanding the levers opens the door to deliberately remodeling the gut community.
europmc-pmc6710438: Autism's roots run deep in DNA - hundreds of genes contribute, each adding a little risk. This review surveys the genetic causes and modifiers of autism spectrum disorder: inherited variants, fresh mutations, and how they perturb brain development. The genetic map is still filling in, but its outlines now guide research.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-38: Covering the 2007 tax filing season, this Government Accountability Office report finds the IRS continuing a trend of improvement in processing returns. It also urges the agency to evaluate ways to cut costs and boost voluntary tax compliance. The review balances praise for smoother operations with pressure to do more with less, as the IRS handles hundreds of millions of returns each year.
gao-gaoreports-b-299738: Camnetics Mfg. took its June 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The manufacturer said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the claims. Factory-floor contracts get the same fair-play ruling as high-tech deals.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-538: The Pentagon's computer buying needed grown-up rules in 2007 — GAO's report says the department had to fully spell out how it managed tech investments. The findings demand the written playbook. The report's refrain: billion-dollar systems deserve better than improvisation.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-138: The State Department's watchdog got watched in 2007, and GAO's report examines what the department's inspector general actually accomplished all year. The findings audit the auditor in careful detail, grading its cases and its reach. The report's meta-lesson stands firm: even the watchdogs need watching, and the diplomats' overseer was no exception.
gao-gaoreports-b-299338: Vaden Industries took its March 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the call on the claims. The firm challenged the award, and the ruling tests the protest in full. The bid-law hearing treats every challenger alike. The process stays the same for all.
openalex-w7204993238: After keyhole surgery to clear bile duct stones, surgeons must decide how to close the duct: stitch it directly or leave a T-shaped drain. This updated systematic review, built to PRISMA standards, compares the safety and outcomes of both approaches in patients with bile duct stones. The authors weigh complication rates and recovery. A technical but consequential comparison for surgeons choosing between two established techniques.
openalex-w7204644738: When jawbone dies after radiation or certain drugs, the damage is severe and hard to treat. This paper studies combining vitamin E (tocopherol) with pentoxifylline as a therapy for jaw osteonecrosis. The authors review the evidence for the drug pairing. A specialized medical review of a treatment that offers hope where surgery alone falls short.
openalex-w7161711938: Japan's Juntendo medical school has deep roots. This history study looked at how doctors were trained and how they worked there under its first three leaders. The team dug through archives and old papers. A medical-history piece on a school's early years.
openalex-w7166510838: Septic shock kills, and filtering bacterial toxins from blood was once a great hope. This paper revisits polymyxin B hemoperfusion guided by endotoxin tests, asking why trials failed and what biology says now. The authors separated hype from evidence. A critical-care review of a therapy seeking redemption.
pmc-13453938: A 2026 correction notice for a paper on endothelial integrin-linked kinase deficiency promoting vascular activation and cardiovascular dysfunction. Journals publish formal corrections to keep the record straight when details need amending. This entry preserves the correction as issued.
pmc-13448138: This 2026 qualitative study examined student leadership in undergraduate nursing research — what roles students take, what challenges they face, and how leading research shapes their professional growth. Content analysis of real experiences gives educators a map of what works. The paper argues research leadership builds better nurses.
pmc-13435238: In this 2026 anthropology paper, the authors critique the coloniality of research ethics in biological anthropology — arguing that ethics frameworks themselves carry colonial assumptions about whose bodies and histories get studied. The essay pushes the field to confront power in its own review processes. It is a provocative, reflective piece.
pmc-13420338: In this 2026 cancer immunology paper, pretreating lymphoma cells with BTK inhibitors made them more vulnerable to CAR-T cells in co-culture, by reducing M2 polarization of macrophages — the tumor-friendly immune state. The combination primes the tumor for the cell therapy. The mechanism suggests a practical sequencing strategy.
pmc-13525738: This 2026 case report described a bifid eleventh rib — a split rib — presenting as a dorsal mass in an infant. The congenital variant mimicked a tumor. The case spares future infants unnecessary workup.
pmc-13530838: A 2026 conference poster comparing ulnar collateral ligament reconstruction with palmaris longus versus gracilis autograft in baseball players. The graft choice was head-to-head. The poster reports the outcomes.
pmc-13448438: A 2026 conference abstract (SADA-22) characterizing molecular and clinical features of systemic cancers that spread to the intradural spine. The rare spread pattern was profiled. The abstract presents the characterization.
pmc-13519038: In this 2026 dental materials paper, fracture resistance of 3D printed versus milled zirconia veneers and anterior crowns was compared. The manufacturing methods were head-to-head. The comparison guides the lab.
pmc-13514138: In this 2026 remote sensing paper, a hybrid multi-scale phase-correlation framework registered multi-temporal very-high-resolution images at subpixel accuracy. The precise alignment enables change detection. The framework is the advance.
pmc-13491538: This 2026 paper, "Educators, Not Influencers," captured health content creators' perspectives on research recruitment collaboration. The creators wanted research roles. The perspectives guide partnership.
pmc-13483538: A 2026 Turkish school-based photoscreening cross-sectional study of undiagnosed visual disorders among first-graders, with cost analysis. The screening caught hidden vision problems. The cost analysis supports the program.
pmc-13479938: A 2026 genomics paper with a haplotype-resolved genome assembly of a male greater yam cultivar revealing young sex chromosome structure and evolution. The yam's sex chromosomes were decoded. The assembly is the resource.
pmc-13469338: In this 2026 paper, changes in muscle mass and quality mediated the effect of high-calorie intake on clinical outcomes. The body composition pathway was the mechanism. The mediation is the insight.
pmc-13474938: In this 2026 materials paper, chirality transferred to the magnetic sublattice in a hybrid perovskite — (R)-/(S)-3-fluoropyrrolidinium copper(II) chloride. The handedness reached the magnetism. The transfer is the physics.
pmc-13460238: A 2026 paper showing miR-29c-3p impaired endometrial epithelial cell adhesion via COL4A1/beta-catenin in endometriosis. The microRNA disrupted implantation. The mechanism is the insight.
pmc-13449038: A 2026 paper showing dorsal raphe tau pathology disrupted sleep-wake orchestration and sleep architecture in a sex-specific manner. The brainstem tau broke sleep differently by sex. The disruption is the mechanism.
pmc-13446738: This 2026 evolution paper found divergent thermal reaction norms of the spontaneous mutation rate among populations of the midge Chironomus riparius. The mutation rate's temperature response evolved. The divergence is the finding.
pmc-13439838: This 2026 ecology paper assessed ecological features and sozological status of the thick-shelled river mussel in right-bank Ukraine's watercourses under EU environmental directives (the title is truncated). The mussel's conservation was evaluated. The assessment informs policy.
pmc-13428038: In this 2026 paper, potent and sustained lowering of serum uric acid was achieved by YJH-012-D, a GalNAc-conjugated siRNA targeting xanthine dehydrogenase. The gene silencer treated gout's chemistry. The lowering is the therapeutic result.
pmc-13455638: This 2026 paper introduced Pig Matrix — a matched multiomics 3D regulatory genomics database for evolutionary and comparative analyses in pigs. The pig's regulatory genome was databased. The matrix serves comparative genomics.
pmc-13401838: A 2026 phase I randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial of olamkicept safety and pharmacokinetics up to 2400 mg in healthy Japanese men. The drug's first human data were gathered. The trial is the safety foundation.
pmc-13387738: This 2026 mechanistic study examined a platelet membrane-coated resveratrol nanosystem in mitochondrial dysfunction and endothelial senescence during atherosclerotic lesion development (the title is truncated). The biomimetic nanoparticle protected vessels. The mechanism is the finding.
pmc-13466938: In this 2026 thyroid cancer paper, the molecular profile of advanced radioiodine-refractory disease and response to lenvatinib treatment was characterized. The resistant cancer's genetics were mapped. The profile guides therapy.
pmc-13529838: This 2026 study found spoken language delay in toddlerhood predicted late childhood language outcomes in dyslexia — evidence from retrospective parent report. The early delay forecasted the later struggle. The predicting aids early identification.
pmc-13570338: A 2026 poultry nutrition paper on partial replacement of soybean meal with brown mushroom stem powder — effects on laying performance, egg quality, and serum biochemistry of laying hens (the title is truncated). The mushroom stems fed the hens. The effects are the finding.
pmc-13492838: This 2026 trial tested unified protocols for transdiagnostic treatment in improving depression, stress, anxiety, emotion regulation, and cognitive symptoms (the title is truncated). The unified therapy worked broadly. The effectiveness is the evidence.
pmc-13453038: This 2026 paper examined digital transformation and green total factor productivity — a contingency perspective on spatial and social embeddedness. The digital-green link was modeled. The examining is the economic insight.

arxiv-2606-16038: Training AI agents to write software is expensive, so researchers distill big models' skills into smaller ones. Open-SWE-Traces advances that process: it releases execution traces — step-by-step records of coding work — to teach software-engineering agents in two modes and many languages. The open release is meant to make agent training cheaper and more reproducible.
arxiv-2606-16138: Dice-math rules (SDEs) sketch shaky systems — stocks, genes, storms. New no-sim trainers learn them straight from facts, skipping pricey fake runs. This paper seals the math gap in those trainers so the short cut stays true. For dice-model builders.
arxiv-2606-16238: Gas-flow math (Navier–Stokes) rules air, fumes, and star clouds. This math paper proves the flow code runs clean for all time — one true path, no blow-ups — even where the gas thins to nil, if one key gauge stays small. For flow-math pros.
arxiv-2606-16538: A pure math paper building a 'pluripotential operadic calculus' — a new toolkit blending field-flow math with operads (frames for mixing steps). The author sets up the frame for experts in algebra and shape math. Thin evidence; the details belong to experts.
